objective: Autonomously implement the complete docs/planning/2026-10-09/implementation-plan.md, P00 through P14, preserving existing functionality and all acceptance requirements. Maintain detailed epics, tasks, implementation steps, acceptance criteria, status and evidence in delivery/tasks.json using delivery/track.py; repository files replace Atlassian, Rovo and Jira. Resume the earliest incomplete phase, delegate independent work to subagents only within that phase, and have Codex review actual results. Use focused local test/debug/fix cycles, then pass the required phase verification, commit and push to feat/agentmux-platform-rearchitecture, and verify the remote commit before advancing. Complete all phases and prove safe bilateral orchestration between independently enrolled real hubs, including automatic Docker Compose startup/reuse and origin-owned result acceptance. Record final Codex acceptance and verify the final branch push without requiring Ryan or Nick. Do not merge. Apply WSL-CLIENT-01: Windows owns Windows-installed AI clients, updates, authentication and configuration; WSL launchers invoke the same installation while Agentmux runtime, Docker Compose and tmux remain Linux-based. Qualify version/update parity, paths, callbacks and isolated concurrent sessions with actual-host evidence and no credential copying. Every Windows-installed client exposed in WSL uses a stable command symlink to its Windows entry point or forwarding launcher; auth/config resolve to Windows-owned files without manual synchronization.
tracking: Use delivery/tasks.json as the authoritative task ledger; use delivery/track.py for status transitions and generated views. No Atlassian, Rovo or Jira installation, authorization or external issue creation is required.
parallelism: Subagents may work concurrently only on tasks in the current phase. Codex integrates and reviews their work; later-phase implementation waits for the current gate.
completionBoundary: All P00–P14 acceptance and required environment checks, task evidence and final agent-operated hub proof are complete and reviewed, final branch commit is pushed and remote identity verified, worktree clean. Merge is outside this objective.
preservedRequirements: All existing capabilities remain in scope; no missing environment or mocked proof is silently counted as a pass.
Product runtime authorization, tenant isolation, human approval when product policy calls for it, evidence and non-destructive tool restrictions remain enforced.
NATS backbone and preferred shared authority; protected plugin kernel; language-neutral extension contracts; automatic Docker Compose startup; actual supported client and hub evidence.

WSL-CLIENT-01: Windows-only client updates and Windows-owned auth/config; stable WSL invocation of the same client, correct arguments/paths and WSL hub callbacks, explicit unsupported interop and isolated concurrent sessions. Native macOS/Linux runtime support remains required.

history.addedExecutionPolicy: When concurrent edits occur, qualify an immutable source snapshot with before/after hashes, then compare the final working and staged bytes. Preserve newer work and historical failures. Recheck affected changes rather than repeating unrelated suites against a moving checkout.

executionPolicy: Resume from current repository state and the earliest incomplete phase. Inspect changed sources and relevant evidence; avoid restarting completed research or repeating valid work.
Keep one active phase. Give subagents bounded tasks with separate file ownership, dependencies and expected evidence; Codex integrates and reviews their results.

Use the smallest relevant failing check during local debugging. Reuse prepared dependencies and isolated fixtures; rerun failures first, then affected integration checks. Run all required phase checks on the stable candidate.

Reuse source-bound evidence only when code, configuration, dependencies, environment and tested assumptions remain applicable. Changed assumptions require new verification; missing required evidence never counts as a pass.

Update task status, blockers and evidence as work changes. Preserve IDs and history; regenerate task views after a coherent set of updates. Rebuild presentations only when their source changes and at review checkpoints.
Batch independent reads and checks. Keep edits, dependent operations and state updates ordered. Prefer actual implementation and defect resolution over repeated status narration or planning churn.

At each phase gate, review full scope, preservation, failure/recovery and supported-environment evidence. Commit, push and verify the candidate before starting the next phase. Keep unresolved findings explicit.

At final acceptance, verify every required deliverable, real-hub bilateral execution, unchanged non-destructive inputs, correlated results and artifacts, final remote commit and clean worktree. Never substitute mocks or reduced scope for required proof.

When concurrent edits occur, qualify an immutable source snapshot with before/after hashes, then compare the final working and staged bytes. Preserve newer work and historical failures. Recheck affected changes rather than repeating unrelated suites against a moving checkout.
